subject.title: Codex turn fails with generic Telegram fallback when invalid image tool model is configured, leaving child agent orphaned on full stdout pipe

question: Should explicit image-generation model refs be rejected during config/startup validation, normalized by doctor, or allowed until tool execution with clearer Telegram diagnostics?
rationale: The remaining fix crosses config compatibility policy, provider/model ownership, Telegram error disclosure, and Codex process cleanup proof, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Validate explicit refs plus diagnostics
options.body: Reject or doctor-repair explicit unknown media model refs before user turns when provider catalogs can prove they are invalid, and keep Telegram diagnostics clear but non-sensitive.

options.title: Runtime diagnostics only
options.body: Keep permissive config loading but convert tool-time invalid-model failures into clear user-facing error ids and log pointers without blocking startup.

options.title: Defer pending live repro
options.body: Wait for a current-main Telegram/Codex reproduction before changing validation or process lifecycle behavior.

recommendation.title: Validate explicit refs plus diagnostics
recommendation.body: Reject or doctor-repair explicit unknown media model refs before user turns when provider catalogs can prove they are invalid, and keep Telegram diagnostics clear but non-sensitive.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue spans image-generation tool ownership and Codex app-server lifecycle history where this owner has the broadest prior commit trail.
